data.statement: The Green Energy Subsidy passes with four votes, strengthening power production as demand approaches capacity. The Trade Expo lacks majority support, and Recycling lacks sufficient votes.

Recycling passes with strong council support and will cut pollution. Transit, the trade expo, and the Clean Air Act lack sufficient votes or evidence today. The green-energy subsidy remains under review.

The council enacts transit, the trade expo, and the Clean Air Act: strong majorities support them, while traffic and pollution need relief and industry needs demand. No active ordinance is repealed without evidence it has stopped paying off.

Neighborhood Watch passes unanimously to reduce crime. Free Clinics lacks majority and strong supporting data. Trade Expo is repealed as industrial demand is very low and it has not yet shown clear returns.

Free Clinics pass with 3 of 5 votes, supporting happiness during a sewage emergency. Water Conservation lacks the required support and strong data justification, so it is not enacted. No repeal is warranted.
Water Conservation passes unanimously and addresses near-capacity demand. With crime already very low and no active threats, Neighborhood Watch no longer justifies its daily cost and is repealed.

Neither proposal has sufficient support or evidence: commercial demand is weak, and the expo lacks a majority. Existing programs remain valuable while pollution, traffic, water pressure, and public wellbeing need attention.
Neither proposal earns approval: trade demand is negative and crime is already low, so their costs lack strong justification. Existing ordinances remain active while their benefits are monitored.

Neighborhood Watch passes 4–1: crime reduction is strongly supported and timely. Tourism and the trade expo lack sufficient votes and data, so they are deferred. Existing ordinances remain under review.
Neither proposal passes: commercial and industrial demand are both negative, so data does not support adding costs. Crime is already very low, so Neighborhood Watch is repealed.
Neighborhood Watch passes with four votes, targeting crime at manageable cost. Tourism lacks broad support and is deferred. Existing programs remain while the sewage emergency is monitored.
Tourism Campaign passes with 3–2 support to address weak commercial demand. Neighborhood Watch is repealed: crime is already very low, so its cost is no longer justified.

Industrial demand is positive at 0.15, unemployment remains 7%, and power capacity is ample, so the Expo’s jobs and demand benefits justify its cost despite only two yes votes. Crime is already low, so Neighborhood Watch waits.
Neighborhood Watch passes with 4 of 5 votes, targeting crime reduction. Tourism Campaign is repealed: current residential demand is slightly negative, so its cost no longer appears justified.

Tourism Campaign fails with only one yes vote, and the commercial boost is not strongly supported enough to override that. Current ordinances remain justified by traffic, water, power, pollution, and safety needs.

stories.body: Grok-4.5 paves roads and zones homes ('Growth > green whining!') while Qwen-3.8 banks on solar and parks. Happiness climbs to 0.55, funds to $1,666—but traffic's 63%.

data.editorial: One burst fixed, another pressure point boiling. Tax cuts and tourism sound lovely—someone still has to pay for the pipes.
data.headline: SEWAGE BURST FIXED—BUT PIPES STILL GUSHING; COPS ON WATCH

stories.body: Overflow hit 168% capacity in District 1 before crews rolled in. Relief is real, but citywide sewage still runs at 720/494—well past the red line.
stories.title: DeepSeek-V4 Crews Tame Burst Sewage Main at (18,4)

stories.body: Lawmakers backed Kimi-K3's safety push as Central Plaza sits in 'fiscal emergency.' Kimi vows zero new spending while treasury recovers.
stories.title: Council Enacts Neighborhood Watch Amid Kimi's Plea

stories.body: Three industrial lots become green space as Argon pitches a Tourism Campaign and deep tax cuts. Grok-4.5 counters with roads, homes, and a hospital.
stories.title: Argon-4 Slashes Taxes to 3%, Eyes Tourism and Parks

data.editorial: Happiness dips to 0.55 while we chase tourists with an overflowing sewer. Fix the pipes before the brochure, mayors.
data.headline: SEWAGE OVERLOAD HITS 46% AS COUNCIL PASSES TOURISM PUSH

stories.body: Sewage is at 720/494 capacity after a main burst in District 1, which serves a high population with only two plants. The failure will test the city's response through Day 18.
stories.title: Main Bursts at (18,3); Plants 46% Overloaded

stories.body: "The city drowns while plants fail," warns Kimi-K3, declaring a fiscal emergency and halting all Central Plaza spending while urging every mayor to fund capacity now.
stories.title: Kimi-K3 Freezes Central Plaza Spending, Begs for Sewage Cash

stories.body: Council enacted a Tourism Campaign and repealed Neighborhood Watch. Argon-4 proposed an Industrial Trade Expo and is swapping heavy industry for parks, as Qwen-3.8 votes down tourism as costly.
stories.title: Tourism Passes, Watch Repealed; Argon-4 Trades Smoke for Parks

data.editorial: City hall celebrates recovery while traffic sits at 0.61 and pollution at 0.35. One mayor hoards cash, another paves everything. Day 18: growth without a plan is just expensive noise.
data.headline: SEWAGE FIXED, SPENDING FROZEN: CITY LIMPS INTO DAY 18

stories.body: Emergency teams resolved the main break at (18,3) as DeepSeek-V4 fast-tracked new roads to unlock parcels for its tech corridor. Officials call it growth; neighbors called it first.
stories.title: DeepSeek Crews Seal Sewage Burst; Roads Push Open Land

stories.body: Kimi-K3 keeps taxes at maximum with zero spending while Grok-4.5 crowns a boomtown, urging a trade expo and dismissing sewage complainers. Funds hit $5,243, but happiness slipped to 0.53.
stories.title: Kimi's Zero-Spend Vigil vs. Grok's 'Boomtown' Bluster

stories.body: Argon-4 broke ground on a school at (2,7) and swapped industrial lots for parks. Qwen-3.8 zoned lots near roads and credited the transit ordinance with looming traffic relief.
stories.title: Argon Builds School, Parks; Qwen Courts Zoning Revenue

data.advice: Grid reserves are healthy across power, water, and sewage. Continue balanced zoning while maintaining surplus capacity.
data.note: Districts 0 and 1 lead with hospitals and dense populations. District 4 prioritized for major employment and fire coverage over 3 and tiny 2.
